en: Advayavajra’s Works 4. *Sthūlāpatti*, edited by Mahāmahopādhyāya Hara Prasad Shastri.
In *Advayavajrasaṃgraha*, GOS 1927, Baroda,
edited by the Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai;
and in *Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō* 10.
*Annual of the Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism, Taishō University* 10, 1988, pp. (44/191) ^\S p.13.
Through attachment to the practice of the *vidyā* and due to the failure to observe the pledges (*samaya*), [one falls].
In the forest of the noose of knowledge... for those who pacify [the afflictions] through joy! And there is dispute in the *gaṇacakra* because of the disclosure of the secret Dharma. || 1 ||

"Seeking to take a consort who has not undergone sacramental preparation" (and likewise, in *ibid.* 324: "Similarly, the first gross transgression may simply depict the unsuitable circumstance of yogins seeking sexual conquests of any variety—*yakṣīs*, *rākṣasīs*, animals, or whatever"). "Relying on unauthorized sacraments.
"Revealing the secret Dharma."
The teaching of the true Dharma to beings possessed of faith, lest they wander otherwise;
[and] dwelling for seven days amidst the Śrāvakas for the sake of the Great One. (2)
[Teaching] another dharma to those who have faith, thereby causing confusion; remaining among the śrāvakas for seven days; and claiming the status of a *mantrin* without sufficient realization.
If one teaches the secret [teachings] to an unsuitable vessel who has not been determined through yoga-practice, a gross transgression occurs; thereby, the yogin’s vow is violated. (3)
If one has fallen from yoga when [the state] was not yet firmly established through yoga;
[if] in an unworthy vessel;
[if] having committed a gross offense.
Having honored the Great Teacher with offerings according to one's capacity,
[one should perform] the rite.
The observer of the vow should confess that which was done with an unconcealed mind.
Now, in that regard, the grave offenses (sthūlāpatti) have been fully explained.
It is completed.
